keyFindings.description: The Go cache figures in the sentence an operator sizes issue_volume from are wrong by about 2.5x, and the same document contradicts them 600 lines later. :1197 and :1819-1820 give the Go build cache as 297 MB and the module cache as 192 MB 'for this repository'; :1801, this branch's own recorded live proof, gives 751 MB and 375 MB. Measured by me at this head in this issue's reviewer container, into an empty pair at /legion/scratch/reviewer/goproof/{build,mod} with GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE exported there: `cd packages/daemon && go build ./...` exits 0 in 114 s and `du -sh` answers 752M build, 375M module. That is one Go module of two — packages/envoy is not in it — and no test has been run. The 297/192 pair came from a different repository. The sizing sentence exists to stop a full disk and the human's open ask 0983e1d7 is read from it, so the wrong figure is a defect of this change: the change is what put the sentence in its current form.

names.go, the canonical pod-paths comment for the issue volume's layout, still says each role's scratch holds 'its temporary directory, its cache, data and state homes, the two Go caches and bun's install cache (roleEnvironment)'. The push that moved the Go pair to /legion/go did not touch this file, so the one block a reader goes to for the volume's layout now contradicts manifest.go:719-731 and manifest_test.go on the only point this push changed, and /legion/go — a new top-level directory of that volume — is named nowhere in it. The same class, smaller: scripts/e2e/README.md's `pod-baseline` row enumerates what checkPodBaseline asserts and was updated for the new state-home path, but not for the TMPDIR assertion the same push added to that function (the file's only TMPDIR mention is at line 215, TMUX_TMPDIR in an unrelated row).

The two sentences a future reader uses to decide whether a new value goes per role or per issue are both false. roleScratch's doc says the split is 'one per role, since the role containers of an issue pod share nothing but the pod' — they share the workspace path, the in-memory config home, uv's cache and Pythons, and, as of this push, the Go pair. And manifest.go:788-790, repeated at manifest_test.go:612-614 and in docs/kubernetes.md, says bun's cache stays per role because 'one cache shared between two roles' checkouts is the cross-checkout corruption --backend=copyfile and the cache per role exist to bound (LEGION-198)': there are no two checkouts per issue. workspace.Location(stateDir, repository, issue) (internal/workspace/provision.go:151) has no role component and every role of an issue works one clone, so the per-role split bounds the number of caches, not the corruption — all six roles install into one node_modules. This is a wording finding, not a reopening of the human's open ask 964174d5: the decision is his, but its premise as written in the code is wrong, and the ask's own 'for that one role, on that one issue' rests on the same premise (reported to the architect, whose text that is).

The reformulated drift fence's opening sentence claims more than the test proves. 'Every directory the runtime tells a role to write in is one the shim makes, and every directory the shim makes is one the runtime names' — the reverse direction is keyed on scratchRoot (manifest_test.go:719), so an issue-shared directory added to roleEnvironment beside the Go pair and not to podsafety.ScratchVariables renders green, which is the shape this push itself introduced. I ran the other mutation to bound the claim: dropping GOCACHE and GOMODCACHE from ScratchVariables IS caught — TestEnsureScratchMakesEveryDirectoryTheRoleIsToldToWriteUnder fails while ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ and ./cmd/legion/ both stay green — so the fence has not regressed for the old axis, only failed to grow for the new one. Narrow the sentence to what the test proves, or key the reverse check on TreeRoot minus the paths the runtime names explicitly.

checkPodBaseline's new TMPDIR assertion, the live half of my round-one finding, is weaker than the mechanism two lines above it. It reads agent["TMPDIR"], refuses only when it is empty, and runs `test -d` on it; it never compares the value. The regression it exists to catch — the runtime no longer setting TMPDIR, so the agent falls back to the image's /tmp — passes both checks. The `want` map at :175-179 already pins XDG_STATE_HOME to roleStateHome(claim.RoleArchitect) and is compared by the loop at :185-190: `want["TMPDIR"] = roleScratch(claim.RoleArchitect) + "/tmp"` is one line there and strictly stronger, leaving only the `test -d` existence check in the shape the profileDir block already uses.

Two stale statements the same push falsified. socketpath_test.go:44-45 says 'cmd/legion answers the same break with a socket directory rooted at /tmp (socketDir, worker_shim_test.go); this package's socketPath does not' — shim_test.go:395 now does exactly that, so a reader of internal/shim is told the package still binds under TMPDIR and will re-derive the sun_path analysis or fix it twice. And podsafety.go:209's rejected-alternative argument counts 'forty-two mount entries' for a subPath mount per directory, which was 7 x 6 roles before this push and is 5 per-role x 6 plus 2 shared = 32 now; the number is the whole weight of that paragraph.
